# Files that are allowed to differ from the upstream react-native tarball of the
# same base version. Anything else differing, added or missing fails the gate.
# One tarball-relative path per line; '#' comments and blank lines ignored.
package.json
scripts/cocoapods/rncore.rb
scripts/cocoapods/rndependencies.rb

# iOS CJK IME composition, cause 7a of https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/56082.
# These are compiled into React.xcframework, not from node_modules, so they only take
# effect through the fork's own prebuilt release - see README.md.
Libraries/Text/TextInput/Multiline/RCTUITextView.mm
Libraries/Text/TextInput/Singleline/RCTUITextField.mm
React/Fabric/Mounting/ComponentViews/TextInput/RCTTextInputComponentView.mm

# `StatusBar.currentHeight` as a lazy getter instead of a class field, see
# https://github.com/react/react-native/issues/41663. Under the New Architecture the
# TurboModule constants are only valid once the module instance exists, so evaluating
# them while this module is being loaded crashes the app on Android - and `import
# {StatusBar} from 'react-native'` alone is enough to trigger it (that is how
# @react-navigation/native-stack uses it). The .d.ts is generated from the Flow source
# at build time, so it differs as well.
Libraries/Components/StatusBar/StatusBar.js
types_generated/Libraries/Components/StatusBar/StatusBar.d.ts

# Sticky headers commit their animated translateY into the Fabric ShadowTree so that
# `measure()` - and the Pressability responder region derived from it - knows where the
# header actually is. The listener driving that commit was attached to an interpolated
# node, which never receives native value updates (only `AnimatedValue` starts that
# subscription), so on Android a tap with any finger movement inside a sticky header was
# cancelled. This subscribes to the scroll value instead. No .d.ts entry - the file
# exports no types.
Libraries/Components/ScrollView/ScrollViewStickyHeader.js
